searchText: Will the BAL EEST tests get updated to reflect the changes here? https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10817 Basically the leading zeros should be removed from slots in the tests. ### EIP-7928 Breakout happening in 5 min: https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/88902627473?pwd=lP4ukflb96wx8f0jc4EWaSUPbr7adn.1 related to this EXTCODECOPY issue https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/1825, do we want to record the destination address in the BAL if the size is zero? It seems like we shouldn't but currently do cc <@792404665068158998> <@796570016966770688> <@762919002196410400> yeah we do want to include it because the state read occurs even if the size of the code is zero hmm it doesn't seem to in nethermind codebase unless I'm missing it, might be an optimisation how would you know that the code size is zero without reading the account from the db? I don't mean the code size, I mean the length which is passed as the last argument to the opcode. If that's 0 we don't need to read the destination address Good edge case, as account gets warmed in any case, it should be put inside BAL. In that case maybe we should still include it if we get OOG on memory expansion (the issue I linked)? The account is warmed before we check for OOG So you're saying that if `EXTCODECOPY` is called with a size of 0 basically nothing happens and we don't need to read the address? I think thats a pretty nice optimization we could include if it doesn't have any edge cases > In that case maybe we should still include it if we get OOG on memory expansion (the issue I linked)? The account is warmed before we check for OOG Memory expansion happens before loading of account, not sure if this logic is correct > So you're saying that if EXTCODECOPY is called with a size of 0 basically nothing happens and we don't need to read the address? It is not nothing, that is my point, you need to warm this account in any case regardless if len is zero or not warming means loading from db could you explain why we would need to load the address even if we don't copy anything `size` 0? It would be consensus bug if you dont do it. Rule as itself does not matter, but following the rule is what is important. so you're saying its because this is defined in a EIP, not because of technical reasons? This way of loading of account was done from inception of EVM, it would be consensus bug if we change it. This is what i think that it should be included in BAL This is code part: https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/blob/88298dbb9da6a523aa997fa1723b20bfc9b57acc/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/host.rs#L149-L182 <https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/blob/77abd37dbd1280a131626cea00b40056a9d39cc1/crates/interpreter/src/interpreter/shared_memory.rs#L530-L533> You load the account for gas accounting but otherwise you don't do anything It does not update the memory, but loading of account does happen and it is read from db and put to inner evm journal state, in case of revm. It is considerd warm loaded after that. Dont want to make a exception and edge case out of this Yeah, I get were you're coming from, just trying to wrap my head around it Yeah, it would be a lot of work and break a lot of assumptions for revm. Would be best if we can just skip loading if len == 0 but this is consensus change to the instruction behavior. We do have to think about these types of edge cases, because with BAL we are enshrining them even deeper into the protocol So if we are enshrining a "unoptimized" version then its at least good to know about it cc <@792404665068158998> <@628018527470616606> I'm told you guys want to move BALs out of the payload. If it's just to not store it and not have it part of the hash, the cleanest solution is to put it on the payload envelope in ePBS ``` class ExecutionPayloadEnvelope(Container): payload: ExecutionPayload execution_requests: ExecutionRequests builder_index: ValidatorIndex beacon_block_root: Root slot: Slot blob_kzg_commitments: List[KZGCommitment, MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK] block_access_list <------------------------------------------------------------------- here state_root: Root ``` So its stored on the CL? no it won't be if the idea is not to store it it does not make sense to store them either way. If we need to store them temporarily we can do this, but I would prefer if the EL does it cause it's a black box to us we can send the list and the payload on the call to `notify_newPayload` ELs still need to store it as the CL requests it to serve the ExecutionPayloadEnvelope later? It's not like the Envelope is a ephemeral comtainer? cc <@363800010518822915> we're storing a blinded payload envelope correct? if we just add BALs there and not change our code we will be storing BALs forever right? <@808969530608451584> my understanding is that now we are storing the CL requests we store everything from the above except the payload For historical blocks, I think there needs to be a way for CL to backfill without downloading the BAL. Should only ever download BAL for blocks within the WSC? System Blobs incoming if BALs are are added to this structure I would also remove them from the thing we commit to db. So there are only two options: 1. We send the BALS to the EL to store and do whatever they want. And we need to add a method to recover them when serving full envelopes. 2. We keep the BALS and store them separately like we do blobs or similar. jinx system blobs without peerdas and size limits <@543900561460822016> I don't think we need BALs are all to sync consensus. The question is to serve blocks, how long do we need to keep envelopes and serve them we do need the CL requests to advance our state. So those are important. BALs we can drop well you need them to send newpayload to EL from WSC until head? For someone forward syncing yes. For checkpoint sync not at all 🙂 checkpoint sync _should_ start from WSC but yes, for a payloadByRange call we will need to have BALS somewhere not saying that is what people do I'm not sure that's true, but let's not get into that one :), we need to cover that range call so definitely BALS need to be available from WSC The other problem is that we will need to at least store the root if we want to verify the signature on the CL when processing blocks Yeah there's the root of the BAL (`block_access_list_root`) in the EL payload header: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4526/files I think there's two things we need to be aligned first and foremost: 1. Do we want to remove BALS from the payload? (this is up to you guys) 2. If the answer is yes, where do we save them? CL or EL? I propose we scope the discussion to quickly agree on those two and then we can discuss the minutiae. At a high level is more or less clear the tradeoff: if we keep them on the EL we need methods to recover payload and BALs by range, etc. If we keep them on the CL we can just send them on new Payload but now we need to be caring about their timeline. So if we are enshrining a "unoptimized" What is an EL payload header? 😉 Gloas kinda removes them The root needs to be in the envelope when storing the BAL within the `ExecutionPayloadEnvelope`, but dropping them any time later we can't really verify the Envelope signature anymore without "hacking" in the root. So I think we need some kind of Union field here.. The previous `CompatibleUnion` type had a way to do this, as something like `CompatibleUnion[1:BlockAccessList,2:BlockAccessListRoot]` would hash to the same root regardless of the variant used. no, we store the blind object like what we do already, we replace the payload by its root Anyway, I think that <@543900561460822016> is pointing correctly in the topic that if this can be store outside of the body but still in the payload like receipts then this should be handled completely within the EL yea, that'S working out because you can restore the ExecutionPayload from the el when you need the unblinded ExecutionPayloadEnvelope. but when dropping the BAL completely at some point, we need to separate it from the ExecutionPayloadEnvelope, otherwise apis break To me, the complexity is that receipts are _never_ provided to the STF whereas with BAL we do want to provide to STF. So this is where we need to figure out how the CL propagates it to the EL. It works trivially as it is currently spec'd because every beacon block stores the entire BAL as part of the ExecutionPayload, but that is wasteful since you only need the BAL at head (and potentially recent past, up to WSC) so the question is: how do you gossip the BAL via normal CL block distribution, but in a way that doesn't download the BAL during back filling? SSZ doesn't really have a way to on-the-fly if you're going to have the full item or if you're just going to serialize the root of a specific item and full value for other things (AFAIK) `CompatibleUnion` had a way to do this, as it didn't hash in the variant in it's first version. But yea, the latest version hashes in the variant too. To add to today's breakout call, now at 60m gas limit, the BAL size (snappy compressed) increased to a median of 84 KiB. Compared to 30m or 36m, this is a sublinear increase as expected (cannot be superlinear). cc <@628018527470616606> The reads / state location contribute around ~30% of the BAL size. Back filling doesn't need the payload envelope so it doesn't matter where you put it ah okay i see! To me it's really a matter of deciding this first To me it feels like the main argument for removing them from the payload is reducing disk footprint, but would this actually the case? I assume the EL would store enough to have BALs within the WSP and can drop older ones. if CL deletes the execution payload, does it matter if the BAL is in it? I think we agreeed on the footprint will be BALS up to the WSP, the question is who holds it if BAL is in the payload the EL will need to keep it. If BAL is out of the payload, and in the envelope, then we have an option, could be CL or EL, not clear which one is better because we need to serve the payload by range queries? yes, payload by range will need to fully recover the payload meaning the envelope but what is the period that we need to serve this? i thought it was just for weak subjectivity period yes correct that's why I say that the footprint is already set okay then it seems fine for EL to keep it for that period In that case you guys just need to decide if it's in the payload (outside the body for example) or in the envelope and we will send it to you with the payload that means that we will store a blinded payload envelope as we do today, but will blind not only the payload but also the bal This sounds like keeping it in the payload is the simpler approach? It's also what we have spec'ed today
